context: Each row begins with unsorted input on the left. A right-pointing arrow labeled with the ordering rule leads to the sorted result on the right. The diagram compares inputs and outputs without showing the internal operations.
description: Names are compared character by character in lexicographic order. The five names here begin with different letters, so their first letters determine the order. Grades follow the custom order D < C < B- < B < B+ < A < A+, from lowest to highest, rather than ordinary ASCII lexicographic order. B-, B, and B+ are three distinct grades. The table lists all the data in the same top-to-bottom row order as the figure.

frames.explanation: Sorting changes only the order of the elements. The chosen comparison rule determines the output.
frames.title: Ordering rules for different data types

summary: Three rows compare inputs and outputs for integers sorted in ascending numeric order, English names in lexicographic order, and grade strings in a custom order from D to A+.

tables.caption: Ordering rules and data before and after sorting for all three rows
